[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we're going to run through the renewal and the IMEA onramp for Velour. Jonas thanks for leading for your side.
[00:18] Jonas Reed: yeah thanks Maya, appreciate it. We've got Amira and Samir and Rae on the line, we'll jump into the details. Rough ask is we need about 2x capacity for peak search & triage flows and to bring up Dublin and a UAE pilot region for latency sensitive routing.
[00:40] Amira Boulos: and to add, our Q4 rollout expects a steady 120 rps per service and peaks to 450 rps for a few minutes during batch windows so cost and latency both matter.
[00:58] Ravi Patel: got it, yeah that profile helps. quick question, are you currently on hosted or dedicated?
[01:05] Jonas Reed: we're on the Redwood hosted tier now, small reserved commit. It's worked well but the peaks are where we get throttled and then fall back to smaller models and that adds jitter.
[01:22] Maya Chen: right, so two levers: we can bump reserved capacity (dedicated pool) or add burst tiers on hosted. Dedicated gives predictability and better SLO isolation; hosted burst is cheaper short-term but less isolated.
[01:40] Rae Park: if we go dedicated what's the lead time? Our infra team is sensitive to procurement windows.
[01:47] Lena Ortiz: dedicated pools typically provision in 4-6 weeks, but for IMEA it can be a little longer depending on capacity in the region. we do have a hybrid pattern where we reserve baseline and allow burst to hosted in the target region.
[02:05] Samir Gupta: security question — for IMEA pilot we need KMS integration and audit logs to meet our regional compliance. can you confirm key rotation and HSM support?
[02:16] Ravi Patel: yes, Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and HSM-backed key configs, though the hosted burst path will use our managed keys unless you opt for VPC/Private. I'll follow up with the exact KMS policy snippets, and we can include them in the security pack.
[02:33] Jonas Reed: can you send the SOC2 scope doc as well? our security team will want that before final signoff.
[02:38] Maya Chen: absolutely. I'll drop the SOC2 summary and the security whitepaper after the call — link to be included in the next steps.
[02:48] Amira Boulos: on latency, we want 95th percentile under 120ms for the user-facing ML endpoints in Dublin. Do you think that's achievable with the hosted option?
[02:59] Ravi Patel: rough answer: yes for single-turn generation at medium tokens if you use local region routing and enable prefix caching. For the larger 8k token prompts (like your diagnostic summaries) you'll want either dedicated or quantized variants to hit that 95th SLO. hosted can hit it during off-peak but peaks will widen latency tails.
[03:25] Jonas Reed: if we quantify — what's the cost delta to guarantee 95th p95 < 120ms with dedicated vs hosted burst?
[03:33] Maya Chen: I'll put together a short table but the ballpark is dedicated baseline ~30% higher monthly commit compared to pure hosted, but reduces per-token latency variance and gives billing predictability. Burst tiers add 10–25% on top of hosted when used heavily.
[03:49] Rae Park: procurement will ask about contract length. Do you have flexibility on term? We might want 12 months but with a 3-month review.
[03:57] Lena Ortiz: yes we can do a 12-month with a mid-term review; can add a clause for a one-time capacity adjustment at month 3.
[04:08] Amira Boulos: we also need to know how rollouts + model pinning work so we don't get surprises when you push newer model variants.
[04:16] Ravi Patel: model pinning is supported, and we have automatic fallback policies so if the pinned variant is unavailable we fall back to an approved family. we can also set canary percentages for rollouts. I'll include the rollout doc snippet.
[04:35] [--- 5 minute marker skipped summary talk ---]
[09:45] Jonas Reed: practical ask — can we lock a small dedicated capacity in Dublin for baseline and use hosted burst in UAE? we don't need full dedicated in UAE initially.
[09:58] Maya Chen: yes that hybrid approach is common. we recommend a baseline equal to 60% of your 95th p95 sustained demand and allow burst to cover spikes.
[10:12] Amira Boulos: what about KV cache behavior across regions? we rely on prefix reuse and don't want cold starts when routing to UAE.
[10:22] Ravi Patel: KV cache is local to the serving region; cross-region cache warms are limited. for multi-region fanout you either pre-warm or keep a shared small baseline in each region. There's a tradeoff in cost.
[10:38] Samir Gupta: about data residency: do logs and request payloads remain in-region when using IMEA edge, or do they cross-seat to US control plane?
[10:49] Lena Ortiz: payloads and inference happen in-region; control plane metadata for Private customers can be in-customer VPC. for hosted accounts some metadata may be routed through our control plane in us-east, but we can sign data processing addenda. Samir: we'll put the exact residency guarantees in writing.
[11:09] Jonas Reed: can we run a short benchmark? something that simulates 200rps sustained with 450rps spikes and the 8k diagnostic prompt set.
[11:18] Ravi Patel: yes. Proposed test plan: provision Dublin baseline endpoints, run 200rps steady for 30m then do 10 minute spike windows to 450rps, measure p50/p95/p99 latency and token cost. We'll also run a UAE-hosted burst test to see cross-region tails.
[11:36] Rae Park: timeline for that?
[11:40] Ravi Patel: I'll need 5 business days to provision test capacity and scripts if we get signoff; then we can schedule the run across two days. propose Aug 10–11.
[11:50] Maya Chen: ok, we'll aim for that. Action: Ravi to provision, Maya to send updated quote before Aug 3, Velour to confirm legal timeline.
[12:05] Amira Boulos: one more on billing — can you show a sample invoice that separates reserved commit, burst usage, and data egress? finance will want line items.
[12:16] Lena Ortiz: yes we can provide a mock invoice; we'll include token breakdown, egress, and reserved vs burst lines.
[12:27] Samir Gupta: security follow-up: if we use hosted burst for UAE, do you provide customer-managed KMS keys for at-rest encryption?
[12:36] Ravi Patel: not for hosted-managed bursts — those use Redwood-managed keys. Customer-managed KMS is available on Private/VPC deployments only. If that is a blocker, we should scope a Private pilot in UAE.
[12:50] Jonas Reed: that might be a blocker for some contracts. Samir, can you assess whether managed keys are acceptable for pilot?
[12:58] Samir Gupta: I'll check with legal and get back by Friday.
[13:05] Amira Boulos: regarding model variants — we sometimes need 8k context but cheaper compressed variants are ok for 60% of requests. Can we route cheaper variant for non-critical flows?
[13:15] Ravi Patel: yes you can set per-route model mappings, and Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization profiles for your workload. We'll suggest an A/B mapping to limit cost.
[13:30] Rae Park: what's the SLA for failover if a region has degraded performance? We need automatic fallback to nearest healthy region within X seconds.
[13:40] Lena Ortiz: failover times depend on routing TTL in your infra; Redwood's smart routing can detect unhealthy endpoints and reroute within 10–30s, with a configurable threshold. We'll include recommended TTL and healthcheck settings.
[14:02] Jonas Reed: ok that's helpful. Last commercial question — any discounts for committing 12 months plus a small upfront payment?
[14:12] Maya Chen: yes we can structure a blended commit with a modest uplift for the dedicated baseline and offer a volume discount for the first-year commit. I'll add a tiered breakout in the quote.
[14:25] Amira Boulos: perfect. What are the next steps?
[14:30] Maya Chen: recap — we'll (1) send quote with burst tiers and EMEA add-on by Aug 3, (2) provide SOC2 + KMS + rollout snippets now, (3) SE to provision test endpoints and schedule benchmarks Aug 10–11, (4) Velour to confirm legal timeline by Aug 5.
[14:46] Jonas Reed: good, thanks all.
[14:49] Samir Gupta: thanks, talk soon.
[14:52] [meeting closed]
